source: Not a book section. The topic follows CodeHS Introduction to Game Design 4.6 and the book's chapter 6.10 (sound and music in games). Structure only: no CodeHS text, problems or code is copied.

lessons.title: Sound in a sketch
lessons.objective: Students will be able to load a sound once, play it with play() or loop(), set its volume and rate, and explain why a browser may stay silent until the player clicks or presses a key.

lessons.title: Sounds on events, music and variety
lessons.objective: Students will be able to play a sound where its event happens once, loop a tune under a game with a volume and a mute key, and vary a sound with a random rate or a random pick from a list.

lessons.title: Music that follows the game, and settings that remember
lessons.objective: Students will be able to change a game's music in the one function every change of screen goes through, and save and load sound settings so a saved 0 is kept.

lessons.title: Check, and make it yours
lessons.objective: Students will be able to explain play against loop, the browser's sound rule and a saved 0, and extend their game with a sound rule of their own.
